status: Post-mortem in: the picture is a three-quarter view
camera: One front camera matched to the reference; every render is scored from it.

arms.name: Six crops
arms.how: Six parallel jobs. Each sees only its crop and models that sixth, then the parts are assembled.

arms.name: Full view, parallel
arms.how: Six parallel jobs. Each sees the whole figure but owns one chunk.

arms.name: Sequential, top down
arms.how: One chunk at a time, head to feet. Each job sees the full image and everything built so far.

arms.name: Feet up
arms.how: Sequential, starting from the feet so the stance sets the scale.

arms.name: Torso out
arms.how: Sequential, starting from the chest so the mass sets everything else.

arms.name: Face last
arms.how: Sequential, big masses first, then limbs, with the face and hands as the final detail pass.

arms.name: Anatomy first
arms.how: Sequential, torso out (the winning order), but every job also sees the Midjourney turnaround (side, back) and measures real depth from an MPFB human body posed with Rigify to his stance; scored from front, side and back.

arms.name: Meshy hero
arms.how: Meshy image-to-3D from his picture (task 01a167ca, 30 credits, about 40 s, no texturing). Not a recipe: the target the scaling version learns from. It came out square to his body, which showed his picture is taken from 24 degrees round.

arms.name: Scaling version
arms.how: The best model so far. Meshy's own mesh, driven by rings per named part and taken to about 3,000 faces; edit it in body words, build it at any polygon count. It edits what Meshy built; learning to build it ourselves is round 5.

findings: Every arm matched his front outline at about 95%: from one picture the outline is easy, the depth is a guess.
Torso out (D2) leads: lowest loss and the best side profile. Sequential beat parallel, but only slightly, and parallel (B) was 3.6 times faster.
Six blind crops (A) were the worst on loss and needed the most fixing at the seams: jobs that can't see the whole man disagree about depth.
Feet up (D1) was worst: starting from the feet set a stance the torso then had to fight.
The Midjourney turnaround showed the real gap: seen from the side, round-1 arms missed 24 to 30% of his profile (calves, back, head).

Anatomy first (E) wins all round: side profile up from 0.76 to 0.87 by taking depth from the turnaround and joint heights from the MPFB + Rigify body (knee, ankle, elbow, wrist within 2 cm). It gave up a little on the front (0.93 vs 0.96) and reads boxier, so the next round keeps E's skeleton and depth and takes D2's front shapes.

Meshy (M) made the most believable 3D man of all, in 43 seconds, from his picture alone. It also showed that his picture is taken from about 24 degrees round, which every hand-built arm had quietly flattened into a square-on figure.

The outline scores undersell M and G. The hand-built arms were fitted to this one camera, and their side and back are scored against Midjourney's guess at a turnaround. Against the Meshy body itself, the scaling version matches 97% to 99.7% from every side, at 900, 3,000 or 9,000 faces.

Rings alone (one stack of 2 cm cuts per part) catch the body but lose the face, fingers and tank-top edges. Using the rings as a cage on Meshy's own surface keeps all of that, and edits by body words still work ('make his forearms 20% bigger').
It scales: brute #2 went through the same scripts with nothing changed (Meshy, learn, cage, decimate) and came out at 3,000 faces with a 98.8% match to its Meshy body from every side.

Evan, 09:24Z: G is the best version by a country mile, but it dresses what Meshy built rather than learning the process. Round 5 keeps G as the bar and learns to build it ourselves: an MPFB + Rigify body plus our recipe parts, named settings fitted against Meshy from every side, then brute #2 from the picture alone.
